meta.drug: ezetimibe (10 mg) + simvastatin (40 mg) vs simvastatin (40 mg) + placebo
meta.sponsor: Merck (Schering-Plough; registry lead sponsor now Organon and Co)
meta.mechanism: NPC1L1 inhibitor (intestinal cholesterol absorption inhibitor) added to statin
meta.modality: small molecule (oral, fixed-dose combination with simvastatin)
meta.indication: secondary prevention after acute coronary syndrome (hospitalized within preceding 10 days)

n_randomized.quote: We conducted a double-blind, randomized trial involving 18,144 patients who had been hospitalized for an acute coronary syndrome within the preceding 10 days
n_randomized.note: Simvastatin-ezetimibe N=9067; simvastatin monotherapy N=9077 (Table 2; registry S3).

median_followup.note: Results: 'After a median of 6 years, 42% of the patients in ...' (premature discontinuation context).

primary_endpoint.value: Composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, coronary revascularization (>=30 days after randomization), or nonfatal stroke
primary_endpoint.quote: The primary end point was a composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, unstable angina requiring rehospitalization, coronary revascularization (≥30 days after randomization), or nonfatal stroke.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Hospitalized for ACS within 10 days; LDL-C 50-100 mg/dL if on lipid-lowering therapy or 50-125 mg/dL if not
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: had LDL cholesterol levels of 50 to 100 mg per deciliter (1.3 to 2.6 mmol per liter) if they were receiving lipid-lowering therapy or 50 to 125 mg per deciliter (1.3 to 3.2 mmol per liter) if they were not receiving lipid-lowering therapy.

planned_events.quote: In the final protocol, we estimated that 5250 events would be required to give the study 90% power to detect a 9.375% lower relative risk for the primary end point with simvastatin–ezetimibe than with simvastatin monotherapy.
planned_events.note: Design paper S4 (pub 2008-09-02): 'Patients will be followed for a minimum of 2.5 years and until at least 5,250 patients experience a primary end point.' Observed 5314 primary events (2572+2742).

assumed_rrr.quote: 90% power to detect a 9.375% lower relative risk for the primary end point
assumed_rrr.note: Unusually small assumed effect, consistent with modest incremental LDL-C lowering (~24%) on a statin background.

power.quote: 5250 events would be required to give the study 90% power

alpha.quote: adjustment of the level of significance to account for the three interim analyses was determined by the Lan–DeMets approximation of the O’Brien–Fleming boundaries for group sequential testing, with a final two-sided P value for significance of 0.0394 or less.
alpha.note: Overall alpha presumably 0.05 two-sided (not stated explicitly). Three interim efficacy analyses at 45.7%, 76.1%, 86.9% of required events.

stopped_early.quote: three interim efficacy analyses were performed, after 45.7%, 76.1%, and 86.9% of the required events had occurred
stopped_early.note: Ran to the target number of events. 'Five amendments to the protocol were implemented during the course of the study, including an increase in the sample size.' Simvastatin uptitration to 80 mg if LDL-C >79 mg/dL (stopped June 2011 per FDA guidance).

baseline.quote: At the time of hospitalization for the index event, the mean LDL cholesterol level was 93.8 mg per deciliter (2.4 mmol per liter) in each group (Table 1).

baseline.note: NOT FOUND (Table S1 of supplement not accessed).
NOT FOUND / not reported in main text.

biomarker_effects.method: NOT FOUND (LDL-C method not stated in main text)
biomarker_effects.quote: Among patients who had blood samples obtained at 1 year, the mean LDL cholesterol level was 69.9 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin-monotherapy group and 53.2 mg per deciliter (1.4 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group (P<0.001) (Table S1 in the Supplementary Appendix). This difference of 16.7 mg per deciliter (0.43 mmol per liter) (P<0.001) represented a 24% further lowering of LDL cholesterol level when ezetimibe was combined with simvastatin than when simvastatin was administered alone.
biomarker_effects.note: Control = simvastatin 40 mg + placebo (active background), so 'placebo-adjusted' = vs simvastatin monotherapy. -0.43 mmol/L. CTT check (derived): 0.78^0.43 = 0.90.

biomarker_effects.timepoint: 1 year, with imputation of baseline value for missing (CTT approach)
biomarker_effects.quote: The between-group difference in LDL cholesterol level at 1 year with imputation was 12.8 mg per deciliter (0.33 mmol per liter).
biomarker_effects.note: This is the calculator-relevant ITT difference. -12.8 mg/dL. CTT check (derived): 0.78^0.33 = 0.92 expected vs observed HR 0.936. Authors: 'The hazard ratio for clinical benefit per millimole of LDL cholesterol reduction with ezetimibe in IMPROVE-IT was 0.80, as compared with 0.78 observed with statins in the CTT meta-analysis.' (Discussion)

biomarker_effects.quote: Over the course of the entire trial, the median time-weighted average LDL cholesterol level was 69.5 mg per deciliter (1.8 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin-monotherapy group and 53.7 mg per deciliter (1.4 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group.

At 1 year, levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, non–high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein were all significantly lower in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group than in the simvastatin-monotherapy group (Table S1 in the Supplementary Appendix).
biomarker_effects.note: Direction only; magnitude NOT FOUND (Table S1 not accessed).

biomarker_effects.quote: At 1 year, levels of total cholesterol, triglycerides, non–high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein were all significantly lower in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group
Ezetimibe plus simvastatin (pooled doses) provided an incremental 13.8% LDL-C reduction, 2.4% HDL-C increase, and 7.5% TG reduction compared with pooled simvastatin alone.
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout phase 3 lipid trial (factorial, 2002). Primary variable was 'direct LDL-C'. Ezetimibe 10 + simva 10 = simva 80 alone (44% LDL-C reduction). 'Placebo-adjusted' here means vs statin alone.

biomarker_effects.quote: At the end of the study, the mean (+/-SD) LDL cholesterol level was 192.7+/-60.3 mg per deciliter (4.98+/-1.56 mmol per liter) in the simvastatin group and 141.3+/-52.6 mg per deciliter (3.65+/-1.36 mmol per liter) in the combined-therapy group (a between-group difference of 16.5%, P<0.01).
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout (2008-03-30) imaging trial: no difference in carotid IMT despite LDL-C lowering; raised doubt about ezetimibe before IMPROVE-IT. Abs -51.4 mg/dL derived (192.7-141.3).

biomarker_effects.timepoint: average over median 4.9 years (SHARP; simva 20 + ezetimibe vs placebo)
biomarker_effects.quote: Allocation to simvastatin plus ezetimibe yielded an average LDL cholesterol difference of 0·85 mmol/L (SE 0·02; with about two-thirds compliance) during a median follow-up of 4·9 years and produced a 17% proportional reduction in major atherosclerotic events
biomarker_effects.note: Pre-readout (2011-06-12) outcome trial of the combination vs placebo in CKD (RR 0.83, 0.74-0.94); cannot isolate ezetimibe's contribution.

hr.quote: The Kaplan-Meier event rate for the primary end point at 7 years was 32.7% in the simvastatin-ezetimibe group, as compared with 34.7% in the simvastatin-monotherapy group (absolute risk difference, 2.0 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.936; 95% confidence interval, 0.89 to 0.99; P=0.016).
hr.note: Registry S3: HR 0.936, 95% CI 0.887-0.988, p=0.016 (Cox). Observed RRR 6.4%, below the assumed 9.375% yet significant because of 5314 events. MI HR 0.87 (P=0.002).

events_treatment.quote: Primary end point: death from cardiovascular causes, major coronary event, or nonfatal stroke ... 2742 (34.7) 2572 (32.7) 0.936 (0.89–0.99) 0.016

safety_signals.value: No excess muscle, gallbladder, hepatic or cancer events
safety_signals.quote: Rates of prespecified muscle, gallbladder, and hepatic adverse effects and cancer were similar in the two groups.
safety_signals.note: Table 3 (simva vs simva-eze): ALT/AST >=3x ULN 208 (2.3) vs 224 (2.5); gallbladder AEs 321 (3.5) vs 281 (3.1); rhabdomyolysis or myopathy 28 (0.3) vs 27 (0.3); cancer 732 (10.2) vs 748 (10.2).

safety_signals.quote: Discontinuation of study medication owing to an adverse event occurred in 10.1% of the patients in the simvastatin-monotherapy group and in 10.6% of those in the simvastatin–ezetimibe group.

safety_signals.value: Hemorrhagic stroke nonsignificantly higher with combination: HR 1.38, P=0.11
safety_signals.quote: There was a nonsignificantly higher risk of hemorrhagic stroke with simvastatin–ezetimibe than with simvastatin monotherapy (difference, 0.2 percentage points; hazard ratio, 1.38; P = 0.11), although the number of hemorrhagic strokes was low.

safety_signals.value: Pre-readout efficacy doubt: ENHANCE showed no carotid IMT benefit despite LDL-C lowering
safety_signals.quote: combined therapy with ezetimibe and simvastatin did not result in a significant difference in changes in intima-media thickness, as compared with simvastatin alone, despite decreases in levels of LDL cholesterol and C-reactive protein.
safety_signals.note: Context for pre-readout skepticism about ezetimibe; not a safety signal of IMPROVE-IT itself.

genetics.finding: NPC1L1 inactivating mutations (heterozygous carriers) associated with 12 mg/dL lower LDL-C and 53% lower CHD risk
genetics.quote: Heterozygous carriers of NPC1L1 inactivating mutations had a mean LDL cholesterol level that was 12 mg per deciliter (0.31 mmol per liter) lower than that in noncarriers (P=0.04). Carrier status was associated with a relative reduction of 53% in the risk of coronary heart disease (odds ratio for carriers, 0.47; 95% confidence interval, 0.25 to 0.87; P=0.008).

genetics.finding: NPC1L1 and HMGCR polymorphisms give the same CHD reduction per unit lower LDL-C (2x2 factorial MR)
genetics.quote: the NPC1L1 group had 2.4 mg/dl lower LDL-C and 4.8% lower risk of CHD (odds ratio [OR]: 0.952, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.920 to 0.985)

genetics.finding: CTT: RR 0.78 per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction for major vascular events (calculator benchmark)
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

consensus_explanation.summary: A small but real benefit that matches the LDL hypothesis. Ezetimibe added only ~24% further LDL-C lowering (16.7 mg/dL at 1 year; 0.33 mmol/L ITT with imputation) on simvastatin 40 mg. The CTT relationship therefore predicted only a ~7-8% RRR. The trial was designed for that: 9.375% assumed RRR, 5250 events, 18,144 ACS patients, median 6 years. It detected HR 0.936 (P=0.016), a per-mmol/L effect (HR 0.80) close to statins in CTT (0.78). This showed that non-statin LDL-C lowering via a different mechanism (NPC1L1, also genetically supported) reduces events, and that lowering LDL-C below 70 mg/dL adds benefit. Success depended on a very large, long trial sized for a small effect. No safety penalty.

open_questions: apoB, non-HDL-C and Lp(a) magnitudes NOT FOUND (only direction stated; Table S1 of supplement not accessed). LDL-C measurement method not stated in main text.
Alpha: final two-sided boundary 0.0394 after three interim looks; overall alpha (presumably 0.05 two-sided) not stated explicitly.

Which LDL-C difference to use in the calculator: 0.43 mmol/L (1-year completers), 0.33 mmol/L (1-year with baseline imputation, CTT approach, used by authors for per-mmol HR 0.80), or ~0.41 mmol/L (time-weighted medians). CTT expected RR: 0.78^0.33 = 0.92, 0.78^0.43 = 0.90 (derived); observed 0.936.

Assumed RRR 9.375% and 90% power are from the final protocol as reported in the 2015 paper; the 2008 design paper abstract gives only the event target (5250). Five protocol amendments, including a sample-size increase; the original assumed RRR/power are not captured.
